A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KAN generalization-bound study. Their complete main texts, figures, equations and appendices are readable, allowing retained material to be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 3 and Figure 2 report original SGD experiments on four synthetic regression/classification setups and MNIST and CIFAR-10.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Appendix A.4 adds training/test-loss curves and an original dropout comparison on two synthetic setups.

M1.justification: Appendix A.4 introduces an implemented regularized KAN variant applying dropout at rate 0.1 to activation functions. The original KAN construction and complexity measure remain; the SiLU-plus-spline description supplies implementation details rather than establishing another architecture change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four synthetic setups and MNIST and CIFAR-10 using AlexNet features. The added dropout experiment reuses synthetic setups (i) and (iii), without changing the represented data or task requirements.

E2.justification: New Figure 4 compares regularized KAN with the retained non-regularized KAN on setups (i) and (iii), whereas v1 reports only the original KAN trajectories. Appendix A.1 compares theoretical MLP bounds; it adds no empirical MLP baseline.

E3.justification: The added dropout study introduces a controlled comparison with and without 0.1 dropout using the same network shapes. The original synthetic sample sizes, 1000-epoch budget, losses and AlexNet preprocessing remain unchanged. The newly specified plotting normalization documents an existing procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 substantially extends the original observational complexity/loss-gap analysis. Figure 3 separates training and test dynamics across all six retained datasets, while Figure 4 tests whether dropout reduces both complexity and the loss gap and reports regularized-to-unregularized complexity ratios.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeat counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new concentration bounds are theoretical results, not changes to empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 3–4 add separate training/test-loss trajectories, dropout results and complexity ratios. Appendix A.4 reports loss gaps of 0.33 versus 0.03 for non-regularized versus regularized KAN in setup (i), and 2.41 versus 0.06 in setup (iii). These are new comparisons; the original Figure 2 trends are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds Assumption 6, Theorem 6, Corollary 3 and proofs for sharper bounds under sub-exponential tails. A.3 adds a Rademacher-complexity lower-bound construction for a restricted subclass. v2 also restores a missing addition sign in Corollary 2. These extend the mathematics beyond the retained main results.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal generalization-bound claims remain. Sections 1.1 and 4 add the explicit proposition that the derived complexity measure could guide regularization during network design and training, extending the earlier claim of practical relevance.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 discusses when relative model complexity could favor KAN bounds over MLP bounds. A.4 connects the dropout findings to complexity control and explains why separately normalized complexity curves require ratio plots for magnitude comparisons. The existing future-work limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 newly specifies the implemented SiLU-plus-spline activation formula, the exact normalization of complexity to the final loss gap, and the dropout rate and placement. These improve documentation without establishing that the original implementation or normalization changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Jacot et al. (2018) and Mei and Montanari (2022) as alternative theoretical perspectives. Appendix A.1 develops the comparison with the already cited Bartlett et al. (2017), and Section 3 newly attributes the synthetic functions to Liu et al. (2024c). The central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: Most original prose and proofs are retained. v2 adds explanatory passages and cross-references, renames Section 2.3 from low-rank RKHS to low-rank Sobolev Space, and moves references before the expanded appendix. The original appendix sections become A.5–A.6.

P2.justification: v2 adds two substantial multipanel figures, resizes and relocates Figure 1, and redraws Figure 2 with larger labels, thicker curves and a clarified legend. New Figure 4 has an inconsistent legend saying train minus test, opposite to the loss-gap definition in Section 3.

improvement.justification: v2 improves experimental transparency, adds useful dropout evidence and corrects Corollary 2. However, new Assumption 6 imposes an uncentered moment-generating-function bound incompatible with its strictly positive B(y) for arbitrarily small positive lambda, making the new guarantee inapplicable as written. Together with Figure 4's reversed loss-gap label, these benefits and defects leave the net quality direction uncertain.
